description: VVC's affine motion model decomposed. Where translational MVs send a single (dx, dy) per block, affine sends 2-3 control-point MVs that define a 4-parameter or 6-parameter affine transformation applied to the block. This captures rotation, scaling, and shear — motion modes that translation simply cannot represent. Per sample, the affine MV is derived by linear interpolation from the control points.

sub_mechanisms.name: 4_parameter_model
sub_mechanisms.definition: Affine motion defined by 2 control-point MVs (top-left, top-right of the block). Captures translation + uniform scaling + rotation; 4 parameters total.
sub_mechanisms.why: Most camera motion (panning + zooming) is well-modeled with 4 parameters: translation + zoom + rotation. Sending 2 MVs costs less than 3 while capturing the dominant motion modes of cinematic content.

sub_mechanisms.name: 6_parameter_model
sub_mechanisms.definition: Affine motion defined by 3 control-point MVs (top-left, top-right, bottom-left). Captures the full affine group: translation + scaling + rotation + shear; 6 parameters.
sub_mechanisms.why: Some motion (perspective projection on a tilted plane, shear from compound rotations) needs 6 parameters. Costs more bits than 4-parameter model but covers a larger family of true motions. R-D selection between 4 and 6 picks the right model per block.

sub_mechanisms.name: control_point_MV_derivation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-sample MV at position (x, y) in the block is: mv_x = a*x + b*y + tx; mv_y = -b*x + a*y + ty (4-param) or mv_x = a*x + b*y + tx; mv_y = c*x + d*y + ty (6-param). The (a,b,c,d) are computed from the control-point MV differences.
sub_mechanisms.why: Linear interpolation across the block gives smooth per-sample motion. The affine matrix is determined by the control points; per-sample MVs are derived by integer-arithmetic linear interpolation (no division at decode time).

sub_mechanisms.name: subblock_motion_compensation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Rather than computing per-sample MVs, the block is divided into 4x4 sub-blocks; each sub-block gets ONE MV (computed at its centre). All samples in a sub-block share that MV.
sub_mechanisms.why: Per-sample affine motion would require per-sample interpolation kernel calls — expensive. Per-4x4-sub-block MV is a piecewise approximation; the discontinuity at sub-block boundaries is smoothed by deblocking. ~20x faster than per-sample with negligible quality loss.

sub_mechanisms.name: affine_merge_mode
sub_mechanisms.definition: Inherit affine parameters from a neighbour without signalling them: an affine_merge_idx selects which neighbour (left, above, etc.) to inherit from.
sub_mechanisms.why: If a moving object spans multiple blocks, its affine parameters are coherent across them. Inheritance saves the cost of re-signalling control-point MV differences (~12-20 bits) at the cost of 2-3 bits for the merge index.

sub_mechanisms.name: affine_AMVP_mode
sub_mechanisms.definition: Explicitly signal control-point MVs using AMVP (Advanced MV Prediction) — each control-point MV is signalled as a difference from a predictor MV (which is itself derived from spatial/temporal neighbours).
sub_mechanisms.why: When affine_merge doesn't fit, AMVP signals the MV difference, which is typically small. Costs more than merge but always available.

sub_mechanisms.name: affine_PROF
sub_mechanisms.definition: Prediction Refinement with Optical Flow: after sub-block motion compensation, samples are refined per-sample using the gradient of the predictor and the difference between the sub-block MV and the affine-computed per-sample MV.
sub_mechanisms.why: Sub-block MC has the per-sub-block discontinuity. PROF corrects this with a 1st-order optical-flow refinement — closing the gap between sub-block speed and per-sample accuracy at small extra cost.

sub_mechanisms.name: warp_field_storage
sub_mechanisms.definition: VVC stores derived affine parameters in a 'history-based MV predictor' (HMVP) table so they can be reused by subsequent blocks even when not directly inherited.
sub_mechanisms.why: Affine motion from one object can be reused on later blocks in the same frame (e.g., the camera-pan parameters apply across many blocks). HMVP keeps recent affine candidates available as predictors.

sub_mechanisms.name: affine_size_constraints
sub_mechanisms.definition: Affine mode is only allowed for blocks ≥ 8x8 (or 16x16 in some profiles). Smaller blocks use translational motion only.
sub_mechanisms.why: Affine parameters' signalling cost is fixed; for very small blocks the gain doesn't justify it. Larger blocks have enough samples that affine's flexibility translates to meaningful residual reduction.

sub_mechanisms.name: ATMVP_subblock_temporal
sub_mechanisms.definition: Advanced Temporal MV Prediction at sub-block level: each 8x8 sub-block of a CU inherits MV from the collocated sub-block in a temporal reference, allowing non-rigid motion within the CU.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foliage, water, crowds: motion within one CU isn't uniform. ATMVP captures sub-block motion variability at zero MV signalling cost (the MVs are inherited from the reference frame). Affine handles uniform deformations; ATMVP handles non-rigid motion.

derivation_rules.name: affine_captures_motion_translation_cannot
if: motion includes rotation, scaling, or shear
then: affine model represents it; translation-only model cannot
derivation_rules.why: Translation is a 2-parameter subset of affine's 4 or 6 parameters. Camera zooms, pans, rotations, perspective distortions all require non-translational components. Affine is the next natural model up the parameter ladder.

derivation_rules.name: subblock_MC_amortises_per_sample_cost
if: affine motion is applied via 4x4 sub-block MVs
then: MC cost is ~20x lower than per-sample with negligible quality loss
derivation_rules.why: Per-sample interpolation would call the 8-tap interpolation filter for every pixel. Per-sub-block calls it 1/16 as often (4x4 samples share one MV). The piecewise discontinuity is small (sub-pixel) and smoothed by subsequent in-loop filtering.

derivation_rules.name: affine_merge_saves_signalling_on_coherent_motion
if: adjacent blocks have similar affine parameters
then: affine_merge inheritance saves ~15-20 bits per block
derivation_rules.why: When a moving object spans multiple blocks, its affine parameters are coherent. Inheriting them costs 2-3 bits (merge index) vs ~20 bits (signalled control-point MV differences). Substantial saving on coherent motion.

derivation_rules.name: PROF_refines_subblock_to_persample_accuracy
then: optical-flow refinement closes the per-sample accuracy gap
derivation_rules.why: Sub-block MVs are piecewise approximations of the true affine field. PROF's 1st-order optical-flow correction captures the residual difference between sub-block MV and per-sample MV without re-running the interpolation filter — cheap, effective.

derivation_rules.name: atmvp_captures_nonrigid_motion
if: motion within a CU is non-rigid (foliage, water)
then: sub-block temporal MV prediction captures it without extra signalling
derivation_rules.why: Affine assumes uniform deformation. Non-rigid motion (each sub-block moves differently, not just rotated/scaled) breaks affine. ATMVP inherits MVs from the collocated reference frame's sub-blocks, capturing whatever motion the reference already had.
